name: Redis bundled jemalloc: compiled-in PAGE must be >= the running kernel's page size (default x86-64 build, LG_PAGE=12)
required_postconditions: os_page_detect() <= PAGE, where PAGE == 1U << LG_PAGE is fixed when jemalloc is configured, not when it runs
every ALIGNMENT_CEILING(size, PAGE) rounding in the allocator is a valid rounding for the kernel's real page size
PAGE_ADDR2BASE masking yields an address the kernel also regards as a page base

failure_sink.description: pages_boot writes "<jemalloc>: Unsupported system page size\n" at pages.c:761 and calls abort() at pages.c:763 when opt_abort is set; otherwise it returns true, which fails malloc_init_hard and leaves the process without a working allocator. Redis links jemalloc as its allocator, so this is a startup abort, not a recoverable error.

source_locations.symbol: #define PAGE ((size_t)(1U << LG_PAGE))  - 'LG_PAGE is determined by the configure script' (pages.h:4)
if (os_page > PAGE) {  - the comparison is >, not !=

extraction_limitations: the real constraint is the inequality os_page <= PAGE. This schema's required_page_size is an equality, so the document has to state the stronger claim 'page size == 4096'. For the default x86-64 build the two happen to agree; they do not agree in general (see redis-jemalloc-page-size-lg16.json)
LG_PAGE is a configure-time value and is not visible in the checked-in source; 12 is the value autoconf derives on an x86-64 host

x_campaign.quote:
if (os_page > PAGE) {
		malloc_write("<jemalloc>: Unsupported system page size\n");
x_campaign.rationale: The probe measured page_size 4096 and this build declares 4096, so rule_page_size returns without a finding and nothing else in the request is contentious. This is the control case: the analyzer should be right and quiet.
